q: The ambassador's remarks were deliberately ___, allowing several interpretations.
explain: Ambiguous = open to more than one meaning.

q: That argument doesn't ___ water.
explain: hold water = be logically sound.

q: We must not ___ the importance of public trust.
explain: underestimate = think something is less important than it is.

q: Her proposal was met with widespread ___.
explain: A noun is needed after 'widespread'.

q: The council ___ a compromise after hours of negotiation.
explain: hammer out = reach an agreement after long discussion.

q: The lord's claims are not ___ by the evidence.
explain: substantiate = support with proof.

q: He tends to ___ around the bush instead of answering directly.
explain: beat around the bush = avoid the main point.

q: The decision will have far-___ consequences.
explain: far-reaching = wide-ranging. (far-fetched = unlikely)

q: Her ___ analysis exposed several flaws in the plan.
explain: incisive = sharp and clear-thinking.

q: The debate became increasingly ___, with insults on both sides.
explain: acrimonious = angry and bitter.

q: With ___, it's clear the plan was flawed from the start.
explain: hindsight = understanding after the event.

q: The treaty was a ___ moment in the kingdom's history.
explain: pivotal = crucially important.

q: She ___ her opponent's argument point by point.
explain: dismantle an argument = take it apart.

q: His apology seemed ___ rather than sincere.
explain: perfunctory = done with minimum effort, as a formality.

q: Let's not jump to ___.
explain: jump to conclusions = decide too quickly.

q: The new policy aims to ___ the gap between rich and poor.
explain: bridge the gap = reduce the difference.

q: The minister's comments ___ a storm of criticism.
explain: spark criticism/a debate = cause it suddenly.

q: The report paints a rather ___ picture of the economy.
explain: A bleak picture = depressing, without hope.

q: She has a ___ grasp of constitutional law.
explain: Collocation: a firm grasp of.

q: The two sides remain ___ apart on the key issues.
explain: be poles apart = completely different.

q: His argument ___ on the assumption that people act rationally.
explain: hinge on = depend entirely on.

q: The scheme was ___ from the start by poor planning.
explain: be dogged by problems = repeatedly affected.

q: Which word means 'to make a situation worse'?
explain: Exacerbate = make worse.

q: Her resignation came as a bolt from the ___.
explain: A bolt from the blue = a complete surprise.

q: The proposal received ___ support from all parties.
explain: An adjective is needed before 'support'; unanimous = everyone agreed.

q: The council will ___ the matter at its next session.
explain: address an issue = deal with it.

q: Critics ___ the plan as unrealistic.
explain: dismiss something as… = reject it as not worth considering.

q: He gave a ___ account of events, leaving nothing out.
explain: Meticulous = very careful and detailed.

q: The debate was ___ by a series of personal attacks.
explain: mar = spoil.

q: Public confidence in the council is at an all-time ___.
explain: Collocation: an all-time low.
